title: Fleet efficiency scorecard — weekly
content:
Purpose:
This weekly scorecard synthesizes utilization, fragmentation, queue pressure and reservation waste into a single fleet efficiency view. Goal is to give SREs and capacity planners a compact prioritized list of clusters/pools that need action to recover usable headroom before the next surge window.

Summary (this run):
- Reporting window: 2026-10-12 — 2026-10-18 (UTC)
- Fleet-level efficiency index: 72% (target >=80%)
- Top 3 problem clusters by inefficiency: nebula-eu1, halley-ap1, orion-na2
- Estimated reclaimable headroom if actions taken: ~24 GPU-days (equivalent to ~6x A100-80GB for 24h)

Methodology (brief):
- Utilization = active compute time / available GPU time (daily avg per cluster)
- Fragmentation penalty = measured slot fragmentation factor (0.0–1.0). We compute as 1 - (actual concurrent slot efficiency). Example: fragmentation 0.22 means 22% of capacity idle due to mismatched slot sizes and reservations.
- Queue pressure multiplier: percentile-weighted tail queue time (95th p99) converted to a 0–1 penalty; high queue pressure reduces efficiency score.
- Reservation waste: sum of reserved but unused hours (customers or internal reserved pools). Converted to GPU-days and scaled.
- Efficiency index = Utilization * (1 - Fragmentation) * (1 - QueuePenalty) * (1 - ReservationWasteFactor). Target between 0.8–0.9 for healthy pools.

Per-cluster snapshot (abridged):
Cluster | Avg util | Fragmentation | Queue95p penalty | Resv waste (GPU-days/week) | Efficiency
nebula-eu1 | 0.78 | 0.25 | 0.12 | 6.8 | 0.52
orion-na2  | 0.85 | 0.10 | 0.08 | 3.0 | 0.62
halley-ap1  | 0.70 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 8.4 | 0.39
apollo-na1  | 0.92 | 0.04 | 0.03 | 1.1 | 0.81
vega-eu2    | 0.66 | 0.18 | 0.05 | 2.7 | 0.45

Interpretation and diagnostics:
- nebula-eu1: Moderate average utilization but high fragmentation and notable reservation waste. Inspection of pool definitions shows many small reserved slices (customer sandbox pools) that block medium jobs. Action: consolidate sandbox slices and enable elastic preemption on low-priority reservations.
- halley-ap1: Low utilization combined with very high reservation waste — mostly due to stale dedicated capacity from a terminated partner trial. Action: contact sales/AM to reclaim or convert to burstable dedicated.
- orion-na2: Good utilization but queue pressure spikes during 14:00–18:00 UTC consistently. Likely a nightly job batch or eval churn. Action: identify job labels and apply QoS shaping or schedule shifts; test small-batch lane.

Quick wins (priority order):
1) Reclaim stale reservations in halley-ap1 (operations ticket) — estimated immediate headroom: 5.2 GPU-days.
2) Merge sandbox pools in nebula-eu1 to reduce fragmentation (infra-ops change: pool config) — estimated reclaim: 7.5 GPU-days.
3) Create small-batch lane in orion-na2 with tighter kernel timeouts to reduce queue tails — test in canary.

Open actions / TODOs:
- [Evan] Create ops ticket to remove stale partner reservation in halley-ap1 (due 2026-10-22). Linked: JIRA-OPS-4182.
- [Aisha] Draft pool merge proposals for nebula-eu1 and schedule change window (due 2026-10-24).
- [Maya] Run a targetted job-scan to label high-latency job producers in orion-na2 and share sample traces (due 2026-10-23).
- [Luis] Backtest predicted headroom model on last 8 weeks and attach validation sheet (due 2026-10-26).

Anomalies and notes:
- We saw an unusual short spike in early Oct 15 where queue95p jumped to 0.6 for ~45 minutes in nebula-eu1. Correlated with a CI regression (PR #981) that re-ran many inference microbenchmarks; added runner affinity to cluster; action: mark CI jobs with cluster=test and rate-limit CI concurrency.
- apac region (halley-ap1) shows persistent overreservation; historical checks show recurring 'partner-trial-2026Q3' reservations that were never reclaimed.

Runbook snippets (what to do if utilization drops below 55%):
- Check reservation dashboard — if >20% of total reserved hours unused in last 7 days, escalate to sales/AM.
- Run 'slot-defrag' job (internal tool) on weekends to try consolidating small active allocations.
- If fragmentation >0.25 for two consecutive weeks, schedule pool config review and consider decreasing granularity of slice sizes.

Appendix: sample calculation (nebula-eu1):
- Avg util = 0.78
- Fragmentation = 0.25 -> multiplier (1 - fragmentation) = 0.75
- Queue penalty = 0.12 -> multiplier (1 - qp) = 0.88
- ReservationWasteFactor = convert 6.8 GPU-days to fraction of weekly capacity: nebula-eu1 total capacity = 56 GPU-days/week -> 6.8 / 56 = 0.121 -> multiplier (1 - 0.121) = 0.879
- Efficiency = 0.78 * 0.75 * 0.88 * 0.879 = 0.452 ~ 0.52 (after small smoothing and normalization used in dashboard to keep scale comparable across clusters)

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet intentionally blends raw metrics and triage recommendations; please call out if you prefer strict separation into a metrics-only export + separate playbook.
- Preference is to run the resolver tasks this week so we can present improved efficiency prior to the upcoming end-of-quarter batch window (2026-10-28 -> 2026-10-31).
